text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Investment fund Rodamco in talks with British Barclays Plc on taking over property fund Imry Holdings. (p1)
- Food company Nutricia abandons intended investments in Burma due to bad human rights situation. (p1)
- Automation company Baan expects recently acquired Ford account will not boost turnover in the short term. (p3)
- Paper and packaging concern KNP BT's unit BT Office books Q4 net income of $4.0 million. (p3)
- Royal Dutch/Shell wins communication prize for adjusting its communication policy after the Brent Spar affair. (p3)
- Department store/services group Vendex to sell its 50 pct stake in catering concern Restoplan and Le Grand Bernard. (p3)
- Philips Electronics chief Cor Boonstra says he will be able to chart the company's course next year. (p3)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Labour party PvdA wants more money for families living on benefits. (p1)
- At least 100 jobs to go in restructuring round at Dutch Airlines KLM's headquarters. (p2)
- Amsteram Stock Exchange to introduce 15 minute break in trading if AEX drops more than 30 points. (p2)
- Price of bankrupt textile group Wyers' warrant soars 13,000 pct from Dfl 0.06 to Dfl 8.00. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Consortium of shipowners is considering leaving the Amsterdam port. (p3)
- Car maker Mitsubishi to expand its plant in Born, in the province of Limburg. (p7)
- Dutch PTT (KPN) loses 100 million guilders a year due to inefficient handling of patents. (p33)
- Unions see no problems for a 36-hour working week at chemicals concern Akzo Nobel. (p33)
TROUW
- Pig farmers in the province of Brabant fear ban on export of pigs, because of swine fever. (p1)
- Junior health minister Terpstra does not want to impose tests for genetically-modified soya on food industry. (p4)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Staff of bulk transhipment company EBS divided on agreement between unions and management. (p11)
